knowns.fact: Requirements: clean simple design, light/dark defaulting to system, existing framework, Zac's voice, brief attribution
Where the brain dump describes how Ang works and the files differ, the files are truth (e.g. evidence tiers)
An "extends"-style shared config (e.g. a team's base ang.json) is the team answer to a configurable config path. Sent here to spike as a documented pattern, not built into Ang

2026 docs field mapped: Starlight and VitePress show the strongest health, popularity and GitHub Pages deploy signals; Zensical looks finished but needs Python and is in beta; Mintlify and GitBook host sites on their own platforms. Observations, not a choice
knowns.answers: Which docs framework is best in class and widely liked in 2026?

knowns.fact: Pages' built-in Jekyll (3.10, frozen; best docs theme Just the Docs) gives sidebar and search; Just the Docs follows system dark mode with one extra stylesheet link and no JS (spike). Starlight or VitePress on Pages via a ~37-line Actions workflow meet the brief for $0, at the cost of roughly yearly forced workflow bumps and framework breaking releases. Custom domain on Pages adds ~$10-12/yr; another host adds a vendor and no gain the brief asks for. Zac leans Pages; anything beyond it must justify its burden
knowns.answers: Hosting: what can GitHub Pages do on its own (built-in Jekyll, themes, plain Markdown) against the brief, and how does it compare with a framework on Pages or a domain plus hosting, in money and effort?

knowns.fact: Just the Docs v0.12.0 builds first time on the github-pages gem v233 (32 lines of config and includes); system dark mode via a media-query stylesheet link, no JS, no flicker; 15-line toggle. Zac: a reasonable first outing, clunky edges to clean up in the build; he'll compare once the field is built

Native Pages bundled themes (primer, minima, cayman, slate) build first time on the github-pages gem v233 from 7 lines of config. None has dark mode or search; only minima has nav. Zac: cleaner and less rough than Just the Docs, cayman is his favourite look, but a baseline nav would have to be built in for the site to be usable; missing search is a gap first-time visitors won't notice

Starlight 0.42.8 on Astro 7.4.5 builds first time in about 1.6s from 41 lines of config and code (32 without a link plugin only the spike needs); system light/dark with an Auto/Light/Dark switcher, sidebar, Pagefind search and on-this-page nav all built in. Attribution needs a 6-line footer override. Remark plugins need @astrojs/markdown-remark since Astro 7's new default Markdown engine. Deploy on Pages: a 31-line Actions workflow. No definition lists; callouts need :::note syntax. Zac: his favourite so far — the best design, and nav, search and a layout every developer knows are pluses — but the colours are ugly and would need real tinkering

Visual bake-off done (Just the Docs, native Pages themes, Starlight, VitePress). Zac's pick on looks: Starlight, with VitePress close behind; both share the best design in the field and both need recolouring. VitePress 1.6.4 builds first time from 30 lines (7 of them a footer override, since the default theme hides its footer beside a sidebar), 3.1s builds, 102 MB node_modules, light/dark and local search built in, a 41-line Pages workflow; v2 has been in alpha since Jan 2025
knowns.answers: Visual bake-off: which candidate's look does Zac pick? Same 3 shared pages (spikes/_content/) in each, light and dark; Zac gives his view in his own words and compares the whole field at the end (no per-criterion scores). Done: Just the Docs, native Pages themes, Starlight. Left: VitePress. One session per candidate

knowns.fact: Install is the one-liner curl -fsSL https://github.com/zacbraddy/ang/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh (or releases/download/{tag}/install.sh for a set version); prerequisite Node 26+ with npm/npx. No uninstall command: removing Ang by hand is a docs page this site owns

decisions.decision: Frontrunners are Starlight and VitePress — Zac rates their designs best in the field and close enough that looks don't decide between them; Starlight is his pick if looks alone decided
